biggestContribution.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: Superset
biggestContribution.text:
🎉 New Investment: Superset 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Superset alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
Superset is the open-source, terminal-first IDE built for the AI agents era. As developers shift from writing code line by line to orchestrating coding agents like Claude Code and Codex, the old text-editor model breaks down. Superset lets engineers run multiple agents in parallel, automate workflows, aggregate context from tickets and logs, and review changes fast.
The traction is remarkable. In just five months since launch, Superset has crossed 11K GitHub stars with 75+ contributors and become a daily driver for engineers at OpenAI, Google, and Vercel, along with major open-source projects like Homebrew and browser-use. It hit number one on Product Hunt and reached the top four on Hacker News twice, backed by a fast-growing community.
The team behind it is Avi Peltz, Kiet Ho, and Satya Patel. They are building exactly where software development is heading and have already shipped a product that the best engineers love and use every day. They move fast, listen closely to their community, and have earned deep conviction from top builders across the ecosystem. I'm thrilled to back them.

biggestContribution.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: Apollo Atomics
biggestContribution.text:
🎉 New Investment: Apollo Atomics (YC P26) 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Apollo Atomics alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
Apollo Atomics builds compact nuclear reactors for customers who can't wait for the grid. Conventional nuclear takes over a decade and roughly $20B per plant, while most SMR startups bet on exotic fuels and supply chains that don't exist yet. Apollo keeps the pressurized water reactor technology that already powers 80% of the world's nuclear plants and redesigns just one component, the steam generator, making the plant roughly 80% smaller without compromising power. The result is a factory-built reactor that fits on a truck and deploys in under 24 months, serving data centers, industrials, and utilities. They've already built and tested a working demonstrator.
Co-founder and CEO Assil Halimi holds a PhD in Nuclear Engineering from MIT, with 18 peer-reviewed publications and two patents on reactor design. He previously worked in reactor operations at Engie and an advanced reactor designer with EDF, the world's largest nuclear operator. Co-founder and COO Drew Walker previously co-founded Blue Innovations Group, an electric boat startup, and served in the White House. Deep nuclear engineering credibility paired with commercial and operations execution. Exactly the team this industry needs.
Let's goo!

🎉 New Investment: Complir 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Complir alongside Y Combinator.
Complir is AI-native compliance infrastructure for global retailers — Vanta for physical products. Selling across markets is brutal: rules differ by country, documentation is fragmented, and regulations shift constantly, so every launch becomes a fire drill. Complir maps products to the right regulatory requirements, turns messy product data into audit-ready records, and auto-generates labels, warnings, risk assessments, and technical docs. When rules or products change, updates propagate automatically. It already manages 100,000+ products and is growing ~45% month over month.
Founders Gustav Bang, Tine Kühnel, and Marc Kaa Brejner have rare founder-market fit. Just a month after Gustav and Tine met, they landed Flying Tiger Copenhagen and embedded inside its compliance, packaging, and sourcing teams for over a year. That ground-level view showed them exactly how compliance breaks — and how to fix it.

biggestContribution.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: InsForge
biggestContribution.text:
🎉 New Investment: InsForge 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in InsForge alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
InsForge is the backend platform built for AI-native development. Backend tools today assume a human at every step, with dashboards and manual configs. As coding agents become the primary builders, that model breaks down. InsForge gives an agent one consistent CLI to deploy and operate the full backend: servers, database, auth, and storage. Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors, while branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes keep changes safe to review or discard. An agent can build, run, debug, and scale an app end to end.
Hang Huang and Tony (Yaowen) Chang are a strong fit for this. Hang, the CEO, is a former Amazon product manager and former pro League of Legends player. Tony, the CTO, was a network infrastructure engineer at Databricks. Together they pair deep infrastructure depth with the conviction that coding agents will soon run entire applications on their own.

evidence.text:
🎉 New Investment: Apollo Atomics (YC P26) 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Apollo Atomics alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
Apollo Atomics builds compact nuclear reactors for customers who can't wait for the grid. Conventional nuclear takes over a decade and roughly $20B per plant, while most SMR startups bet on exotic fuels and supply chains that don't exist yet. Apollo keeps the pressurized water reactor technology that already powers 80% of the world's nuclear plants and redesigns just one component, the steam generator, making the plant roughly 80% smaller without compromising power. The result is a factory-built reactor that fits on a truck and deploys in under 24 months, serving data centers, industrials, and utilities. They've already built and tested a working demonstrator.
Co-founder and CEO Assil Halimi holds a PhD in Nuclear Engineering from MIT, with 18 peer-reviewed publications and two patents on reactor design. He previously worked in reactor operations at Engie and an advanced reactor designer with EDF, the world's largest nuclear operator. Co-founder and COO Drew Walker previously co-founded Blue Innovations Group, an electric boat startup, and served in the White House. Deep nuclear engineering credibility paired with commercial and operations execution. Exactly the team this industry needs.
Let's goo!

They are building exactly where software development is heading and have already shipped a product that the best engineers love and use every day. They move fast, listen closely to their community, and have earned deep conviction from top builders across the ecosystem. I'm thrilled to back them.

🎉 New Investment: Complir 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Complir alongside Y Combinator.
Complir is AI-native compliance infrastructure for global retailers — Vanta for physical products. Selling across markets is brutal: rules differ by country, documentation is fragmented, and regulations shift constantly, so every launch becomes a fire drill. Complir maps products to the right regulatory requirements, turns messy product data into audit-ready records, and auto-generates labels, warnings, risk assessments, and technical docs. When rules or products change, updates propagate automatically. It already manages 100,000+ products and is growing ~45% month over month.
Founders Gustav Bang, Tine Kühnel, and Marc Kaa Brejner have rare founder-market fit. Just a month after Gustav and Tine met, they landed Flying Tiger Copenhagen and embedded inside its compliance, packaging, and sourcing teams for over a year. Every primitive returns structured outputs and readable errors, while branching, scoped permissions, and reversible writes keep changes safe to review or discard. An agent can build, run, debug, and scale an app end to end.

evidence.title: Taro Fukuyama new investment: Limrun
evidence.text:
🎉 New Investment: Limrun (YC P26) 🎉
I'm excited to share that I'm investing in Limrun alongside Y Combinator and Pioneer Fund.
AI coding agents now write software in the cloud, but their Linux sandboxes can't run native mobile toolchains. No Xcode, no reliable Android emulator, no clean way to build and ship iOS or Android apps. Limrun fixes this with remote Xcode, iOS Simulators, and Android Emulators that any cloud agent can call through a single skill file. An agent goes from ticket to fully tested, preview-ready pull request without ever leaving its sandbox. You can now use it with any background agent. Quizlet and Sorce are using Cursor Cloud with Limrun to build their mobile apps. Replit, Rork, and vibecode.dev already build on it, and Limrun is now opening the platform to every mobile team.
Limrun is built by Muvaffak Onuş, an emeritus maintainer of the CNCF project Crossplane and former tech lead at Upbound. He most recently led AI infrastructure work at QA Wolf, where he saw firsthand how today's sandboxes break down at scale. Few people understand cloud-native infrastructure for agents this deeply, which makes him exactly the right founder to build the mobile execution layer for the agent era.

▫️ Standout (YC P26) — a hiring marketplace where autonomous agents represent both candidates and companies.
▫️ Superset — the IDE for running hundreds of coding agents in parallel.
